plan: First playable: a ring of four big glowing pads with distinct pitches that replays sequences growing from one to eight notes, slowing down after mistakes. No speed mode, scores or extra pads.

First playable: six illustrated hand drums from different cultures that sound on any tap, over three gentle backing loops with an optional echo pattern to copy. No scoring, recording or timing judgement.
First playable: four piano lanes with falling note tiles for 10 public-domain melodies, a slow practice speed and a note-name strip on the keys. No song import, endless mode or leaderboards.

First playable: one beat line with big targets for quarter, half and eighth notes over 8 short tracks, latency calibration and a no-fail mode that shows notes as fractions. No charts editor or combos.

First playable: a small keyboard where the player hears and matches illustrated intervals and major or minor chords across 12 graded sets, scheduled by spaced repetition. No scales, notation or singing.

First playable: an 8-step by 5-row pentatonic grid where tapped notes loop and each row grows its own singing plant, with free play and 8 short melody challenges. No scale switching, export or chords.

First playable: a tiny orchestra plays 5 short pieces whose tempo follows the conducting arc traced on visible beat markers, with instrument sections that can be cued. No full scores or free composition.

First playable: 8 familiar songs with a scrolling pitch line and a singing character; microphone pitch feedback is opt-in and off in kids mode, with a tap-along fallback. No recording, sharing or scoring.
First playable: two link friends trade four-beat dance phrases on a glowing beat circle; the player copies each call with taps across 10 songs, with no fighting and a no-fail mode. No online duels.
First playable: 12 auto-scrolling levels where the hero hops across stepping stones spaced to a visible four-beat rhythm, with latency calibration and slow mode. No level editor or free movement.
